body:
The round was led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. All existing investors, including QED, Greenoaks, Lightspeed, Hedosophia and Bek Ventures, participated in the round, alongside new investors Galdana Ventures, Cogito Capital, Inveready and Invus, and leading European entrepreneurs Tomas Okmanas and Didac Lee. This round brings the company’s total funding to more than $515 million.

Founded in 2018 in Sofia by Hristo Borisov, Boyko Karadzhov, and Konstantin Dzhengozov, Payhawk is an AI-native spend management platform that orchestrates global money across Bills, Cards, Expenses, Travel, and Procurement for maximum control, automation and savings.

The company plans to move beyond spend management to build an operating system (OS) where AI agents, payments, and enterprise controls run finance together.

_“Through our technology, finance departments can benefit from ‘zero-touch finance’, where neither the finance professional nor the employee deals with any admin work. 77% of our customers use our agents daily across financial control, procurement, travel and reporting to save time and money for their businesses. But AI alone cannot deliver this transformation, it must be combined with a robust payment infrastructure and enterprise controls to truly unlock the potential of every enterprise in the new AI era,”_ added Borisov.

According to the company, ERP systems, banks, procurement platforms, treasury products, travel tools and spend platforms are all becoming more intelligent with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. But Payhawk argues that making each application smarter does not automatically create a smarter finance operation.

_“Integrations connect systems. MCP makes information easier to access. But an operating system changes how the entire finance function works. As software moves from recommending actions to actually taking them, that distinction becomes much more important,”_ stated Borisov.

The company is building its finance OS around three interconnected layers: AI agents that perform financial work; payments infrastructure that lets agents safely interact with money; and enterprise controls that determine what agents can do and when human intervention is required.

Borisov revealed that Payhawk aims to build a global finance category built from Europe. “Europe does not need to build local versions of categories invented somewhere else. We should build categories the rest of the world follows as craftsmanship and innovation are strongly embedded cultural traits for Europeans. We want to build the infrastructure through which businesses around the world run their financial operations in the age of AI. Being born in Europe has exposed us to this complexity from day one. We know what it takes for our customers to stay in control with their businesses spread around the world while scaling and while trying to be efficient at the same time. The window to define that category is open now — and we are moving fast,” he commented.

Headquartered in London, Payhawk now operates across 33 countries and 12 offices, with a platform that spans multiple currencies, banking systems, payment rails, regulations and local practices.

Payhawk reports it achieved positive cash flow in Q3 and still holds 70% of the capital it raised in its 2022 funding round. In March 2022, it raised an additional €89 million and extended its funding to €191 million, making it Bulgaria’s first unicorn.

In November 2021, the company raised €99 million in Series B funding, valuing it at €505 million. It raised €16.5 million in Series A in April 2021 and €3 million in a Seed round in March 2020.

The company notes that its business model relies on predictable subscription pricing rather than card interchange, aligning growth with helping customers save money rather than incentivising them to spend more. The company says this independence also lets Payhawk develop AI-native finance products that work beyond its own cards. In the US, for example, its Financial Controller Agent works with customers’ existing business cards, eliminating the need to switch providers or reissue cards.

_“Payhawk’s exceptional growth reflects the strength of its engineering DNA, global footprint and clear vision for the future of modern spend management systems. As payments, AI and enterprise software increasingly converge, we believe Payhawk is well positioned to emerge as a leader in this rapidly evolving market. We are excited to partner with the team as they continue to scale globally and enter their next phase of growth,”_ said**James Hayward**, Managing Director within Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, who is also joining Payhawk’s Board of Directors.

Rahul is an experience tech journalist and the former Editor-in-Chief of SiliconCanals. In December of 2025 he joined EU-Startups as News Contributor, covering Europe's biggest startup stories on a daily basis.
